title: BlenderBIM build from source on macos (arm64) with `make dist` exits with Error
body:
Building the BlenderBim Add-on from source according to the documentation at https://blenderbim.org/docs/devs/installation.html#building-from-source exits with an `Error`.

System information:
```zsh
➜  ~ sw_vers
ProductName:	macOS
ProductVersion:	12.5.1
BuildVersion:	21G83
➜  ~ arch
arm64
➜  ~ which python
python not found
➜  ~ which python3
/opt/homebrew/bin/python3
➜  ~ python3 --version
Python 3.10.6
```

Starting the build from source with the command:
```zsh
make dist PLATFORM=macos PYVERSION=py310
```

## wrong `python` command 

First try gives an error due to wrong command references in the current `/src/blenderbim/Makefile`:
```zsh
# Provides BIMTester functionality
cd dist/working && python -m venv env
/bin/sh: python: command not found
make: *** [dist] Error 127
```

The `Makefile` refers in 3 occurrences to a `python` command, instead of a `python3` command. `python3` is the default command name for either the system provided as well as the homebrew installed Python v3. This can easily fixed:
```diff
diff --git a/src/blenderbim/Makefile b/src/blenderbim/Makefile
index c9dd15b7..dac9b774 100644
--- a/src/blenderbim/Makefile
+++ b/src/blenderbim/Makefile
@@ -138,7 +138,7 @@ endif
        # Provides IFCClash functionality
        cp -r dist/working/IfcOpenShell-0.7.0/src/ifcclash/ifcclash dist/blenderbim/libs/site/packages/
        # Provides BIMTester functionality
-       cd dist/working && python -m venv env
+       cd dist/working && python3 -m venv env
        cd dist/working && . env/bin/activate && pip install pybabel
        cd dist/working && . env/bin/activate && pip install babel
        cd dist/working && . env/bin/activate && ./env/bin/pybabel compile -d ./IfcOpenShell-0.7.0/src/ifcbimtester/bimtester/locale/
@@ -165,7 +165,7 @@ endif
        mkdir dist/working
        cd dist/working && wget https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/d6/fd/eb8c212053addd941cc90baac307c00ac246ac3fce7166b86434c6eae963/pystache-0.5.4.tar.gz
        cd dist/working && tar -xzvf pystache*
-       cd dist/working/pystache-0.5.4/ && python setup.py build && cp -r build/lib/pystache ../../blenderbim/libs/site/packages/
+       cd dist/working/pystache-0.5.4/ && python3 setup.py build && cp -r build/lib/pystache ../../blenderbim/libs/site/packages/
        rm -rf dist/working

        # Provides SVG export in construction documentation
@@ -283,7 +283,7 @@ endif

        # Required by IFCCityJSON
        mkdir dist/working
-       cd dist/working && python -m venv env
+       cd dist/working && python3 -m venv env
        cd dist/working && mkdir site-packages
        cd dist/working && . env/bin/activate && pip install cjio --target=./site-packages
        cd dist/working/site-packages/ && rm -r *dist-info*
```

## `pystache` error

Second try after fixing the correct python command errors on a `pystache` type error:
```zsh
x pystache-0.5.4/tox.ini
cd dist/working/pystache-0.5.4/ && python3 setup.py build && cp -r build/lib/pystache ../../blenderbim/libs/site/packages/
pystache: using: version '63.4.3' of <module 'setuptools' from '/opt/homebrew/lib/python3.10/site-packages/setuptools/__init__.py'>
Warning: 'classifiers' should be a list, got type 'tuple'
error in pystache setup command: use_2to3 is invalid.
make: *** [dist] Error 1
```

And indeed, pistache v0.5.4 uses a tuple in it's classifiers, see https://github.com/defunkt/pystache/blob/17a5dfdcd56eb76af731d141de395a7632a905b8/setup.py#L129-L143.
This can be fixed by simply updating pystache to v0.6.0 (which doesn't use Classifiers anymore):
```diff
diff --git a/src/blenderbim/Makefile b/src/blenderbim/Makefile
index c9dd15b7..e1bc0f73 100644
--- a/src/blenderbim/Makefile
+++ b/src/blenderbim/Makefile
@@ -163,9 +163,9 @@ endif

        # Provides Mustache templating in construction documentation
        mkdir dist/working
-       cd dist/working && wget https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/d6/fd/eb8c212053addd941cc90baac307c00ac246ac3fce7166b86434c6eae963/pystache-0.5.4.tar.gz
+       cd dist/working && wget https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/3f/e7/8750ba6c6101d6aa5ceeb20c013adf2c6f3554a12c71d75654b468404bfa/pystache-0.6.0.tar.gz
        cd dist/working && tar -xzvf pystache*
-       cd dist/working/pystache-0.5.4/ && python setup.py build && cp -r build/lib/pystache ../../blenderbim/libs/site/packages/
+       cd dist/working/pystache-0.6.0/ && python3 setup.py build && cp -r build/lib/pystache ../../blenderbim/libs/site/packages/
        rm -rf dist/working

        # Provides SVG export in construction documentation

```

## patch rejected

The next error is above my mental pay grade, as it deals with file paths. 

```zsh
cd dist/working/ && patch ../blenderbim/libs/site/packages/behave/model_core.py < model_core.patch
patch: **** rejecting file name with ".." component: ../blenderbim/libs/site/packages/behave/model_core.py
make: *** [dist] Error 2
```

Any idea on that?

title: Add additional quantity calculations to QtoCalculator
body:
Goal of this PR is to augment the QtoCalculator class with functions that mimic the qto abilities of bim calculation software.

For each new function there should be clear docstrings as well as a conceptual sketch of what the formula is calculating (For reference see documents below).  Please give feedback on the maths and code as I update this draft PR.  

Formulas covered so far:

- [x] get_linear_length - already covered by @Moult
- [x] get_volume - already covered by @Moult 
- [x] get_length - already covered by @Moult 
- [x] get_width - already covered by @Moult 
- [x] get_height - already covered by @Moult 
- [x] get_perimeter - already covered by @Moult 
- [x] get_net_footprint_area - already covered by @Moult 
- [x] get_net_top_footprint_area - adaptation of @Moults code by @vulevukusej 
- [x] get_side_area - already covered by @Moult 
- [x] get_area - already covered by @Moult , will be renamed to get_total_surface_area
- [x] get_projected_area - (Includes toggle for choosing net or gross) @vulevukusej
- [x] get_net_side_area - @vulevukusej and @Gorgious56 
- [x] get_gross_side_area - @vulevukusej 
- [x] get_net_top_area - @vulevukusej 
- [x] get_gross_top_area - includes a method for calculating opening methods @vulevukusej 
- [x] GrossFootPrintArea - achieved using get_gross_projected_area @vulevukusej 
- [x] get_side_opening_area - includes filter for opening size @vulevukusej 
- [x] get_opening_type - determines whether opening is a "RECESS" or "OPENING", since sometimes this is undefined. @vulevukusej 
- [x] get_OOB_object - returns the oriented bounding box  @vulevukusej 
- [x] get_AABB_object - returns the axis-aligned bounding box @vulevukusej 
- [x] get_bisected_obj - returns the object bisected by two planes @vulevukusej 
- [x] get_total_contact_area - Returns the total contact area of the object with other objects. @vulevukusej 
- [x] get_touching_objects - Returns a list of objects that are touching the object. @vulevukusej 
- [x] get_contact_area : Returns the contact area between two objects. @vulevukusej 
- [x] get_intersection_between_polygons: Returns the intersection between two polygons. @vulevukusej 
- [x] Width/Height at given height/width - achievable through get_bisected_obj
- [x] Area between two intersection planes - achievable through get_bisected_obj
- [x] Volume between two intersection planes- achievable through get_bisected_obj
- [x] Cross-Sectional Area at intersection - - achievable through get_bisected_obj
- [x] Perimeter Base/IntersectionPlane/Top  - achievable through get_bisected_obj

Considerations to keep in mind:
- Modifiers for formulas, such that users can fine-tune the calculation according to their needs or that of a standard (SMM7, VOB, ÖNORM etc.)
- I think it would be nice if the script could generate a calculation output that allows the user to inspect the calculation. This could be an output using matplotlib for example.
- In cases where no IfcOpeningElements are defined, perhaps we need an algorithm for defining opening meshes such that norm calculations can be performed correctly?  I know iTWO users use this feature regularly @TZwielehner 

The following files are from the iTWO Documentation - In particular, "Element Planning - Geometric Parameters" will probably serve us more than well enough. It's not exactly a concise document, but I commend the original designers who developed such a comprehensive feature.
[Element.Planning.-.Geometric.Parameters.pdf](https://github.com/IfcOpenShell/IfcOpenShell/files/9553940/Element.Planning.-.Geometric.Parameters.pdf)
[Element.Planning.-.Overview.Geometric.Parameter_EN.pdf](https://github.com/IfcOpenShell/IfcOpenShell/files/9553941/Element.Planning.-.Overview.Geometric.Parameter_EN.pdf)

title: Is there an efficient way to reassign class?
body:
I currently use this method https://github.com/IfcOpenShell/IfcOpenShell/blob/v0.7.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/ifcopenshell/util/schema.py#L51-L66 to reassign a class, e.g. from an IfcWall to an IfcSlab. It involves creating a new entity, copying attributes as best it can, swapping all inverse references from the old to the new entity, then removing the old entity.

It's a lot of steps, and I'm running it on large models with many tens of thousands of objects, and it gets impractically slow. Basic profiling shows https://github.com/IfcOpenShell/IfcOpenShell/blob/v0.7.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/ifcopenshell/util/schema.py#L64 replace_attribute to be guilty, which I have no idea how to make simpler (https://github.com/IfcOpenShell/IfcOpenShell/blob/v0.7.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/ifcopenshell/util/element.py#L398-L402 the walk is the bottleneck, it seems, but it is necessary).

Note that it's not just a speed issue, the speed seems to slow down over time, and memory climbs. By the time I've done about 7000 elements I'm starting to run out of memory.

I wonder if there is a more fundamental trick that can be applied here, without the whole recreate and replace, but instead just edit-in-place and even keep the same STEP ID. Any ideas? Maybe old could get a new STEP ID without changing references, and new could use the previous STEP ID?

title: Code to generate window geometry
body:
IFC specifies basic parameters to define the geometry of a standard window. Purely using numpy, the task is to create a function to generate this geometry compliant with the IFC specification. Inputs to this function will be things like overall width, overall height, partitioning type, and so on. Output will be a regular Python dictionary of various 3D coordinates as numpy arrays.

Windows are always rectangular. Windows are always along the XZ plane, where X is horizontal and Z is vertical, and have a depth along the Y axis.

To begin with, only the front-view of the window should be generated. 3D coordinates will still be used, by the Y value will always be 0.

Inputs:

 - OverallHeight (Z dimension) http://ifc43-docs.standards.buildingsmart.org/IFC/RELEASE/IFC4x3/HTML/lexical/IfcWindow.htm
 - OverallWidth (X dimension) http://ifc43-docs.standards.buildingsmart.org/IFC/RELEASE/IFC4x3/HTML/lexical/IfcWindow.htm
 - PredefinedType (the simplest being SINGLE_PANEL) http://ifc43-docs.standards.buildingsmart.org/IFC/RELEASE/IFC4x3/HTML/lexical/IfcWindowTypePartitioningEnum.htm

There will then be a series of lining parameters, described on this page: http://ifc43-docs.standards.buildingsmart.org/IFC/RELEASE/IFC4x3/HTML/lexical/IfcWindowLiningProperties.htm - examples include LiningDepth and LiningThickness. Since we're only looking at the front view for now, for example LiningThickness is relevant but LiningDepth is not. The parameters provided depend on the number and configuration of panels defined by PredefinedType. For example, a SINGLE_PANEL will have no transoms (horizontal dividers) and no mullions (vertical dividers).

Then, there shall also be an input of the following parameters for each panel (the number of panels, and their possible positions are determined at the PredefinedType). Described here http://ifc43-docs.standards.buildingsmart.org/IFC/RELEASE/IFC4x3/HTML/lexical/IfcWindowPanelProperties.htm

For example, an OverallHeight=1200 and an OverallWidth=600 will produce:

```
{"frame": [[0,0,0], [600,0,0], [600,0,1200], [0,0,1200], [0,0,0]], "panels" [ ... ]}
```

Notice how the first coordinate is repeated to indicate a closed loop. Clockwise or anticlockwise is not important. Depending on the number of panels, the panels value will be a list of panels, each with a position and similar rectangle loop coordinates.

I've attached a sample blender file for a single panel window along with sample input parameters. For now, only focus on creating rectangles for the "2D" flat representation. In the future, the code will have to be able to also produce geometry for a 3D representation (the exact method of this geometry shall be specified later).

[IfcWindow.blend.txt](https://github.com/IfcOpenShell/IfcOpenShell/files/9645886/IfcWindow.blend.txt)

(remove .txt extension, it's only there for Github)

title: choco yesterday
body:
I had a closer look at the previous failed and successful action runs and realized, 
that they were all triggered far later than scheduled: 
They were scheduled for 23:55 but actually run between 00:30 and 00:55 - 
so one day later, where usually no bbim release would be there yet. 
But even if, then it would be a release with a high probability to be overwritten 
again during the day, which would cause sha256sum in choco to be off.

So I switch now to - what I think - is a far more robust approach: 

We now run the action well past midnight, but instead just check for **yesterday's** bbim releases. 💡 
With this approach, there are also no more late sha256sum colliding releases possible, as yesterday is really over. 🙂

title: UI Papercuts
body:
Following a comment from @Moult on the OsArch forum I'm opening this thread to centralize the problems (papercuts, not backend or missing features) users have with the interface and find a sensible way to fix them. I don't know if a github issue is the right format but I'll try to update it as we go.

For now, concerning the Type Manager / Type instancer, I have noted :
- [x] The type manager can't be reached from within the N panel UI. I expected the same features to be present in both places
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25156105/200129887-c5028423-12ca-4860-b4e8-2391aa724e74.png)
- [x] The type manager and type instancer can't be reached from the properties editor. You can't add an IfcElement from there but you can modify the instance settings
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25156105/200129942-f582940e-1130-4936-b0ad-41305b730272.png)
- [x] I would change the current BIM tool SHIFT + S shortcut which overwrites a pretty usefull vanilla shortcut to move the 3D cursor or move objects to the cursor. On a side note i think overriding SHIFT + R is fine since this vanilla function seems to mess up with the addon stability.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25156105/200130500-62f45ecc-1264-4b75-b6eb-8173556b0837.png)
- [x] I'd like to be able to drag-select multiple objects (or circle select) in the BIM tool and it's currently not possible. The other tools allow it so there might be a setting that overwrites it somewhere ? 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25156105/200130794-228ae65e-1e05-4023-90ed-ac89853b9df2.png)
- [x] Next a papercut that's been posted on the forum but I can't find it anymore to reply. Not really something that can be solved by Blenderbim since it's a feature of Blender. The "Region Overlap" setting in the preferences prevents you from scrolling horizontally to get to the settings on the right when there are many. Granted it's bad UX in the first place but disabling it solves _this_ problem.
![capture](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25156105/200131405-36a9882a-cf82-4973-9568-a3aacab62f04.gif)
- [x] The type manager has thumbnails. It would be nice if the profile manager also had thumbnails.

title: Feature: express rules
body:
🎅 happy holidays everybody 🎅

This pull request gives us preliminary support in Python for evaluating rules, functions and derived attributes defined in the express schema.

Following our elaborate testing strategy. The behaviour and semantics of the generated rule code has been tested on 104 specifically crafted minimal .ifc files.

It is implemented as a code generation process taking the express ast and rewrite it to python. This works surprisingly well up to some extent:

### query expressions

E.g query expressions are appropriately mapped to python list comprehensions.

```
HasAdvancedFaces : SIZEOF(QUERY(Afs <* SELF\IfcManifoldSolidBrep.Outer.CfsFaces |
  (NOT ('IFC4X3_TC1.IFCADVANCEDFACE' IN TYPEOF(Afs)))
)) = 0;
```

```python
assert (sizeof([afs for afs in self.Outer.CfsFaces if not 'ifc4x3_tc1.ifcadvancedface' in typeof(afs)])) == 0
```

### aggregate literals

List literals are also fairly equivalent:

```
V : IfcDirection
  := IfcRepresentationItem() || IfcGeometricRepresentationItem () || IfcDirection([1.,0.]); 
```

```python
v = IfcDirection(DirectionRatios=[1.,0.])
```

Although the repetition clause needed to be represented using a different syntax:

```
Res  := IfcRepresentationItem() || IfcGeometricRepresentationItem () || IfcDirection([0.0:Ndim]);
```

```python
res = IfcDirection(DirectionRatios=([0.0] * ndim))
```

(notice how the complex entity construction is resolved to a simple construction using named parameters by the schema knowledge embedded into the code generation process)

### static vs dynamic typing

Another complexity was in static typing. The typing on locals was mostly eliminated, but when assigned an aggregate literal we need to assign the correct type:

```
Names : SET OF IfcIdentifier := [];
```

```python
names = express_set([])
```

### inverse roles

Also ifcopenshell provided great fundamentals. The `usedin()` function was easily implemented using `ifcopenshell.file.get_inverse(with_attribute_indices=True)` to easily filter on the roles an entity participates in.

## Complexities

At the same time there were quite a few complexities regarding semantics that made it somewhat harder to use python as the base language for implementing an express rule verifier.

### One based indexing

This was resolved by postfixing every index_qualifier with `- 1`. We didn't simply subtract one during the code generation process because in rules and function indexing can also happen based on variable names (e.g `i` in a loop).

```
MinutesInRange : ABS(SELF[2]) < 60;
```

```python
assert (abs(self[2 - 1])) < 60
```

### Out of bound indexing

Even more difficult was the fact that out of bound indexing in express simply returns indeterminate, whereas in Python an exception is raised. This is actually hard to address because it affects the behaviour of builtin python classes and we also don't want to dramatically affect the behaviour of core IfcOpenShell. Therefore only a workaround is presented when coupled with the exists() function, to defer evaluation of the arguments by wrapping them in a lambda and catching any potential index error in the implementation of the exists() function.

```
WR35 : (
  EXISTS(SELF\IfcPropertySetDefinition.DefinesType[1])) 
  AND 
  ('IFC4X3_TC1.IFCDOORTYPE' IN TYPEOF(SELF\IfcPropertySetDefinition.DefinesType[1])
);
```

```
assert (exists(lambda: self.DefinesType[1 - 1])) and ('ifc4x3_tc1.ifcdoortype' in (typeof(self.DefinesType[1 - 1])))
```

The fact that boolean operators short-circuit (i.e the second component of the `and`-clause is not evaluated when the first component returns False means that no exception in python will be thrown

### Case insensitivity

Case insensitivity is implemented simply by converting all variable cases to lowercase, which is not a fully general solution, but in working state for the rules in the schemas.

# NB: Breaking change!

Note that this PR results into one breaking code change. Derived attributes are now supported, this is more of an addition: attribute names that previously didn't **exist** now do. However, express also allows redeclaring inherited attributes as derived (the `*` in .ifc spf files). In that case previously getattr returned None in IfcOpenShell, but now returns the properly derived attribute, e.g:

```
>>> import ifcopenshell
>>> f = ifcopenshell.file()
>>> f.createIfcSIUnit(UnitType='LENGTHUNIT', Name='METRE') 
#1=IfcSIUnit(*,.LENGTHUNIT.,$,.METRE.)
>>> f[1].Dimensions
#0=IfcDimensionalExponents(1,0,0,0,0,0,0)
```

🎅 happy holidays everybody 🎅

title: Run IfcConvert on sample files in CI/CD
body:
Previously we had this in travis.yml

```
  - |
    (for i in *.ifc; do \
    echo $i | tee -a log; \
    timeout 1m /usr/local/bin/IfcConvert -yv "$i" "$i.dae" --validate >> log 2>&1; \
    echo $i $? >> statuses; \
    done) || true
  - echo Failed
  - grep -v 0$ statuses
  - grep -v 0$ statuses | wc -l
  - echo Succeeded
  - grep 0$ statuses
  - grep 0$ statuses | wc -l
```

it wasn't perfect in the sense that we wouldn't get notified when there were regressions, but still it's a nice metric to have.

title: Using add with a STEP ID cause a segfault
body:
Since this commit https://github.com/IfcOpenShell/IfcOpenShell/commit/d9f1cb5525f57e7b2ea78647c730f74d62405032 there is now a segfault for all of these testcases: https://github.com/IfcOpenShell/IfcOpenShell/blob/v0.7.0/src/ifcopenshell-python/test/api/root/test_reassign_class.py#L24-L44

It segfaults upon calling `ifc_file.add(new_element, element.id())`. Changing it to just `ifc_file.add(new_element)` fixes the segfault, but defeats the purpose of the commit.

Upon reading the commit, indeed it makes no sense to do ifcopenshell.create_entity() (i.e. an entity without an associated file) and then do `replace_attribute` in the context of a file... so I'm kinda not surprised it's segfaulting. Is there a way to "change" the STEP ID after creation? That would be ideal.

Thoughts @aothms ?
